# dsh-tauri-notify-webhook
**English** · 简体中文

Forward a DSH desktop task notification to **email (SMTP)** or **pushplus** — when a task
stops abno
rmally or completes, and only while the window is not in front of you.
## The problem this solves

The desktop shell already shows a toast when a turn ends, and it is easy to miss for a
reason worth

already shows a toast when a turn ends, and it is easy to miss for a
reason worth stating precisely:

- A toast is a system notification. If the window is in front of you, you were already
watching the

answer stream in — the toast is noise. If you walked away, the toast is
gone by the time you come ba

ck, and nothing remains on screen.
- The interesting endings are not equally interesting. A turn tha

t ran to the end needs no
attention. A turn that **errored, was aborted, hit the token ceiling or wa

s blocked** does.
- The host keeps only the **latest** `turn/end` per session, so a finished session

leaves no
queue to read later. Once you were away for that moment, the information is simply gone.

This plugin moves the notification off the screen and onto a channel that keeps history,
and it fire
s only for the two endings you would actually act on.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The same spec works in the GUI plugin panel (**设置 → 插件 → 安装**), which accepts any npm
spec. For a lo
cal checkout, install the directory instead:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

There is no build step at install time: `dist/` is committed. This is deliberate — the
desktop profi

le installs plugins as packages, and a package that has to be compiled after
installation would need
a toolchain the profile does not have.

**Restart DSH.** This is required, not optional: the harness keeps loaded plugin modules in
its load

er cache, and `hmr.root` defaults to `[]`, so a newly installed plugin does not take
effect in a run

and `hmr.root` defaults to `[]`, so a newly installed plugin does not take
effect in a running host.
## Use

Open **设置 → 任务推送**, pick a channel, fill in its fields, press **发送测试**, then
**保存**. The test button

only becomes available once the form differs from what is saved,
so a successful test always descri
bes exactly the values you are about to store.
| Channel | What it needs |
| 邮件 (SMTP) | SMTP host, port, security, from, to; username and password are optional for relays tha

t accept anonymous mail |
| pushplus | A token from pushplus.plus; pushes go straight to the officia

l `/send` endpoint |
| 关闭 | Nothing is sent. This is the default |
## What it does
### Two triggers
| Trigger | Fires when |

| 任务完成 | The turn ended with reason `completed` |
| 任务异常停止 | The turn ended any other way — `aborted
`, `error`, `blocked`, `max-tokens`, `interrupted`, `forked` |

Both are on by default and are switched independently. Sub-agent sessions are skipped: they
are driv
en by their parent, so they would otherwise produce a burst of pushes for one task.
### Only while you are away

A push is sent only when `document.visibilityState === 'hidden'`. The Tauri shell patches
`document.

hidden` to the real window focus state, so this is "the window is not in front of
you" rather than "

the tab is in the background". While you are watching the session, the
plugin stays silent.
### How one push is decided
The client cannot read a turn's ending reason, so the decision takes two round trips:

1. The session list flips a session from `running: true` to `false` — that edge is the only
thing wa

tched, so a session that was already finished when the plugin loaded is never
back-filled.
2. After

a 250 ms settle window (a turn can flicker its running flag), the client asks
`GET /turn-end?session

Id=…` for the reason the host recorded.
3. If the session is still stopped and has not stopped again

in the meantime, the client
posts `POST /delivery`. The host re-reads the settings at that moment a

eantime, the client
posts `POST /delivery`. The host re-reads the settings at that moment and sends.

Every step re-checks that the plugin is still loaded, so a reload mid-flight cannot deliver
a stale

step re-checks that the plugin is still loaded, so a reload mid-flight cannot deliver
a stale push.
## Where your credentials live

Settings are stored on this machine only, at `$DSH_HOME/notify-webhook/settings`
(`DSH_HOME` default

s to `~/.dsh`). The file is written through the shell's atomic-write
helper, so a crash mid-save can

not leave a truncated config. Nothing is uploaded anywhere
except the channel you configure.

The host routes are loopback-only, and every mutating request must also be same-origin;
a browser pa
ge on another origin cannot read your settings or make the plugin send mail.
## Requirements

* The DSH **desktop (Tauri)** shell — this plugin is a client of the shell's `dsh-tauri`
and `dsh-ta

uri-ui` runtime plugins, and of the `settings.section` slot, so it does not
apply to a browser-only

profile.
* Node.js ≥ 22.15.0.
* For email: an SMTP server you can send through. For pushplus: a toke

ofile.
* Node.js ≥ 22.15.0.
* For email: an SMTP server you can send through. For pushplus: a token.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]

CI runs the same four gates on Node 22 and 24, and then asserts that `dist/` is up to date
(`git dif
f --exit-code -- dist`) — if you change `src/`, commit the rebuilt `dist/` with it.

`compat/` holds local stand-ins for the two modules the shell injects at runtime
(`dsh-tauri`, `dsh-

tauri/client`, `dsh-tauri-ui/client`). They exist so that `tsc` and the
unit tests can run outside t

he desktop app; `tsdown` marks those specifiers external, so
none of this code reaches `dist/`.
